correctness.rationale: For mu,g,v,gamma strictly positive, the scalar gap drift is uniformly contracting and the three-state chain irreducible. The stationary mode equations have zero endpoint flux, and integrating them over a boundary layer forces the losing-mode tails to be O(epsilon) and O(epsilon squared) relative to the attracting-mode tail. The remaining scalar logarithmic derivative is beta/epsilon + O(1); integration yields finite positive tail amplitudes and exact density powers. Interchanging modes proves the other boundary. Independent symbolic identities and a conservative finite-volume stationary generator reproduce exponents and conditional mode ratios. These numerical tests do not prove the infinite-dimensional or all-parameter statement.

originality.rationale: The established 2023 active-Dyson work gives the two-body fixed points and one-particle positional singularities; its universal N-gamma/mu positional exponent is not the spacing marginal. The 2021 pair-interaction paper gives a general three-state stationary ODE and explicitly depicts the force 1/y-y, but its analyzed exact densities and exponents are for harmonic attraction; it does not state the two distinct logarithmic-repulsive spacing-edge exponents, their sharp rate interval, or the state-resolved boundary hierarchy. The 2023 follow-up treats weak-noise position covariances, not nonperturbative spacing tails. A 2019 two-state single-particle edge law is not the interacting three-mode claim. The new contribution is a sharp global classification of a natural gap statistic, not the reduction to three modes or the forward equation. Broader implicit coverage via general PDMP boundary theorems remains a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: The 2021 arbitrary-force forward equation is a strong implicit predecessor; specialist literature may contain a general boundary-exponent theorem whose specialization already covers these exponents.
The published active-Dyson particle-position exponent and the new gap exponent must not be confused, and the novelty claim is limited to the exact scoped two-edge classification.
The 2019 confining-potential primary full article was not inspected beyond the accessible abstract.

value.rationale: Nearest-neighbor spacing is the canonical finite-particle interaction observable in a logarithmically repulsive gas, whereas the motivating publications primarily analyze one-particle position densities or weak-noise covariances. The exact two-edge singularity transition is a natural complete classification with distinct measurable accumulation and depletion regimes. A universal reciprocal-rate sum and boundary mode hierarchy quantify a parameter-sensitive structural difference invisible in single-particle exponents; no unmotivated finite slice or merely cosmetic reparametrization is involved.
